clue.text: Unable to fly in cloud

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A grounded bird, or aircraft, stuck in cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to fly' reads as one phrase meaning flightless, so you look for a word like that; split it and 'unable' is the fodder, 'to fly' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space.

clue.text: Broadcaster snorting cocaine — a means of getting high

indicators.note: the broadcaster takes the drug up inside itself

parts.note: a cabler is a cable-television broadcaster
C = cocaine (slang abbreviation)
used literally

explanation.surface: A scandal story about a media figure caught with cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting high' completes the drugs picture, but the definition means altitude: a cable car carries you up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car hauls passengers up steep slopes on an overhead cable.

clue.text: User of special make-up

parts.note: S = special
toner is a cosmetic applied to the skin

explanation.surface: Someone who wears unusual cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User' looks like a plain noun for anyone who uses something; here it is the drug user, and a stoner is a habitual cannabis smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is someone who regularly uses cannabis, a drug user.

clue.text: Hides recipes in Paul's cryptic

indicators.note: the letters are hidden in a puzzling order

parts.note: R = recipe (as on a prescription), so two of them
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Paul, a setter's name, has tucked some recipes away in his crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' is a verb meaning thrashes, not conceals: to hide someone is to beat them. Paul is also a Guardian setter, which makes the surface a wink.
explanation.definitionFit: To larrup is to thrash, as is to hide (tan someone's hide).

clue.text: Spot of Jazz perhaps led by Duke

indicators.note: the Duke's letter goes in front

parts.note: D = duke
Jazz is a variety of apple; 'perhaps' flags an example

explanation.surface: Duke Ellington leading a band in a spot of jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: Jazz next to Duke summons Ellington, but Jazz here is an apple variety, and the capital J is there to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both as verb and noun: a dapple is one of the round patches on a dappled horse.

clue.text: Solitary Shakespearian lover dumping a jerk

parts.note: HERMIA, a lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream, loses her A
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A lonely Shakespeare character who has ditched a creep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' invites the insult, the lout being dumped; it is really a twitch. HERMIA is one of the four lovers lost in the wood in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermitic means like a hermit: solitary.

clue.text: Saint-Saëns a bit lively

indicators.note: the letters are stirred into motion

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A music critic finds a Saint-Saëns piece fairly lively.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen welds 'Saint' to 'Saëns' so you read one composer's name; break it and 'Saint' is the definition, with the rest scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Sebastian is the martyr traditionally shown shot with arrows.

clue.text: Looked at coffee on the counter

indicators.note: counter as in running counter to, going the opposite way

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Eyeing a cup of coffee sitting on a café counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' is where a café serves your coffee; read counter as contrary and it turns DECAF around.
explanation.definitionFit: To face something is to look towards it.

clue.text: Name ships after people from city

indicators.note: the ships come after the name

parts.note: to dub is to name
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: An instruction to name ships after a city's inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name ships after' reads as christening vessels in someone's honour; 'after' is really positional, and 'Name' is a verb meaning to confer a title, as when a knight is dubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain demonym: the city is Dublin, and James Joyce's story collection takes the word as its title.

clue.text: In the mirror, Big Bird starts to prepare shaving foam

indicators.note: a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the emu is a very large flightless bird

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the words prepare and shaving, whose first letters are used

explanation.surface: Big Bird, the Sesame Street character, looks in the mirror and starts lathering up shaving foam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Bird' suggests the Sesame Street character, but it is just a large bird. 'In the mirror' reverses everything: EMU followed by PS, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spume is froth or foam, especially the foam on breaking waves of the sea.

clue.text: Is that Hazel O'Connor finally wearing shirt?

indicators.note: wearing means one thing is inside another, so the letter goes inside the shirt

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of O'Connor

parts.note: last letter of O'Connor

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether that is the singer Hazel O'Connor at last, dressed in a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel O'Connor is a British singer and actress, which makes 'Hazel' read as a first name; here it is the plant, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hazel is a small tree or shrub bearing hazelnuts, so it is one kind of the answer.

clue.text: May Queen overtaking close to traffic sign

indicators.note: overtaking means the queen moves up close behind the letter, coming next in line

parts.note: may and can both express permission or ability

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word, its last letter

parts.note: last letter of traffic
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The May Queen's procession overtakes a traffic sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May Queen' reads as the village festival figure, but splits into May (permission) and Queen (ER). The sign is one of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer, the Crab, is the fourth sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Go through in style introducing wingers for extra time

indicators.note: introducing means the first part leads in and the other follows

parts.note: a perm is a hair style, a permanent wave

indicators.note: wingers are the players out on the flanks, so for each word only its outer letters are taken

parts.note: outer letters of extra
the wingers of time too: its outer letters T and E

explanation.surface: A football team goes through in style, bringing on wingers for extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: 'wingers' are the outside letters of both 'extra' and 'time', and 'style' is a hairstyle; 'introducing' puts PERM in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to pass or spread through something, as a smell permeates a room.

clue.text: Strip clubs having forked out for protection

indicators.note: for protection means the letters of forked shelter the club letter inside them
out means the letters of forked are put out of order

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Strip clubs have paid out for protection money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip clubs' reads as one phrase, but 'Strip' is the definition, a verb, and 'clubs' is the card suit. 'Out' rearranges FORKED, which then gives 'protection' to C.
explanation.definitionFit: To defrock a priest is to strip them of their clerical office, literally taking away the frock.

clue.text: Descriptive words lit up Pete Seeger's first hit

indicators.note: lit means drunk, so the letters reel about

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: take the first letter of Seeger

parts.note: the first letter of Seeger
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Adjectives light up the folk singer Pete Seeger's first hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' reads as illuminated praise; take lit as drunk and the letters stagger. 'Hit' looks like the record but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Epithets are descriptive words or phrases attached to a name.

clue.text: Sea creature caught by Scotsman

parts.note: c = caught, from cricket scorecards
Rab is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A fisherman from Scotland landing something from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' is one phrase on the surface; split it and 'caught' is C and 'by' simply places it next to RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the crustacean with pincers is one of many animals living in the sea.

clue.text: Home counties member eating a fish

indicators.note: the combination takes A inside

parts.note: the Home Counties lie round London in the South East
member = penis, for which cock is slang
used literally

explanation.surface: A member of a suburban club near London tucking into fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated SE for South East. 'Member' reads as a club member; it is the cruder sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea cock is an old name for the gurnard, a fish.

clue.text: Cry of derision about hospital blanket

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around

parts.note: a catcall is a jeering whistle or shout
H = hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Jeering at a hospital's bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital blanket' reads as bedding; 'blanket' is really the adjective, as in a blanket ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all rule, like a blanket one, covers everything.

clue.text: Painter left snail-like tracks

parts.note: L = left
a snail is proverbially slow
RY = railway, which runs on tracks

explanation.surface: An artist leaving a trail like a snail's.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry painted crowded northern English industrial scenes with matchstick people. 'Left' reads as departed; it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Lowry is one particular painter, named here with his initials.

clue.text: Wall Street's direction of travel for 16

definitions.meaning: market jargon: which way share prices are heading, where a market going neither up nor down has its own term
a cross-reference to another answer in the grid, an animal with a famously odd gait

explanation.surface: A market report on where stocks are heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is CRAB, and crabs walk sideways; a market that moves neither up nor down is said to trade sideways, so Wall Street and the crab share a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways is how a crab walks and how a flat market is said to move.

clue.text: Piece from Henri Charrière in supplement

indicators.note: take a piece out of the letters that follow

parts.note: hENRI CHarrière

explanation.surface: An extract from Henri Charrière, author of Papillon, printed in a newspaper supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplement' reads as the magazine section of a newspaper; it is the verb, to add to.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to supplement it, adding value.

clue.text: Manual covering sex toy originally found in pieces

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the pieces

parts.note: chess pieces are known as men
it is an old informal word for sex appeal or sex

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of toy

parts.note: first letter of toy

explanation.surface: A sex toy is discovered smashed to pieces, along with its instruction manual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' looks like a handbook but is the adjective, of the hand. Chess pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a glove with one section for the fingers, so it covers the hand.

clue.text: Root's skied edge produces chaos

indicators.note: a skied ball goes up, and in a down clue up means reversed

parts.note: a yam is an edible root
a hem is an edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Joe Root, the England batsman, skies an edge and causes chaos in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England cricketer, and to sky a ball is to hit it high; neither the man nor the shot survives, since root is a vegetable and skied turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; mayhem was once a legal term for maiming, and now means wild disorder.

clue.text: Sedative drug offence divides American golf

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: divides means the offence splits the pair, sitting between them

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: A sedative drug offence splits opinion on American golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sedative' is used as an adjective, meaning calming, and 'easing' fits that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing describes something that relieves pain or calms, which is what a soothing sedative does.

clue.text: Stripped briefly in front of Echo Beach

indicators.note: in its plain positional sense

parts.note: SHORN, stripped of wool, loses its last letter
E = echo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Getting undressed quickly ahead of a day at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo Beach is a 1980 song by Martha and the Muffins, so the two words read as one name; split, Echo is E and Beach is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both name the strip of land where sea meets dry ground.

clue.text: Buddy possibly disheartened by German army showing spirit

parts.note: HOLLY, as in Buddy Holly, loses its middle L
G = German
a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A friend is dispirited by a German army putting on a show of fighting spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buddy' reads as a friend; it is Buddy Holly, the 1950s rock and roll singer, and 'possibly' flags that Buddy only points to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the third person of the Christian Trinity is also called the Holy Spirit.

clue.text: Pierce Brosnan's heartbeat

parts.note: the surname Brosnan, whose central letter is used
the word splits in two: heart asks for the central letter of Brosnan, and beat gives tick, the beat of a clock

explanation.surface: A fan muses on the heartbeat of the actor Pierce Brosnan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pierce Brosnan' looks like the actor's name, but 'Pierce' is the definition, a verb. The setter splits 'heartbeat': the heart of Brosnan is its central S, then a beat is a TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick a pin into something is to pierce or puncture it with a point.

clue.text: Young boy touring Northern Territory

parts.note: green = young and inexperienced
a lad is a boy
N = northern

explanation.surface: A youngster on a trip round Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Territory' names an Australian region, so the two words stick together; split, Northern is N and Territory the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the vast Arctic island is self-governing but belongs to Denmark, so it is a territory rather than a country.
